title: Low-Documentation Business Funding
seo_title: Low-Doc Business Funding: Bank Statements | Fidelity Funding
meta_description: Low-documentation business funding relies on bank statements instead of tax returns and financials. Learn how it works, what it costs and who it suits.
dek: When tax returns are not filed yet, or the paperwork is the obstacle, bank-statement underwriting can open a faster route. Here is what you trade for it.
intro: A new restaurant has strong daily deposits but only ten months of history. A contractor files taxes that show modest profit after deductions, even though the business account moves $90,000 a month. A seasonal retailer's financial statements are two years behind. For all of them, a traditional loan application can feel like a wall of paperwork that does not show what the business really does.

Low-documentation funding takes a different view. Instead of asking you to prove the business on paper, it studies the money that actually flows through your business bank account. The paperwork shrinks, the timeline shortens, and the underwriting question changes from what your tax return says to what your deposits show.
This guide covers how that works, what is still required, how it is priced and where it fits. Availability and terms vary by funding partner and your profile.

paragraphs: Low-doc does not mean no-doc. It means a smaller, more targeted set of documents. A typical package might include the last three to six months of business bank statements, a government ID, and basic business information. Some partners add a voided check or ask for a brief call.

What you usually do not need are multiple years of tax returns, profit-and-loss statements, balance sheets, a formal business plan, or collateral appraisals. Those are standard requirements for conventional bank loans and SBA programs, and they are a major reason those take longer.

Underwriters read your statements the way a doctor reads a chart. They look at total monthly deposits, the consistency of those deposits, average daily balance, the number of days the balance dips negative, returned items or insufficient-funds fees, and any existing debt payments flowing out.

Many partners calculate a figure often called average monthly revenue by summing qualifying deposits and removing transfers between your own accounts or one-off items like loan proceeds. The funding amount is then typically a fraction of that revenue. Each partner sets its own method and limits, which is why two offers can look different from the same statements.

Low-doc funding is a common fit for businesses whose paperwork understates their performance: owners who minimize taxable income, newer companies with short histories, businesses that handle much of their revenue in cash deposits that do reach the bank, and owners who need speed more than the lowest possible rate.

It is a poorer fit for businesses with erratic deposits, frequent overdrafts, or heavy existing debt, because the statements themselves tell a difficult story. Clean, steady statements are the asset here.

Fewer documents mean the funder relies on fewer data points, so pricing generally runs higher than for fully documented bank loans. Terms are usually shorter and payments more frequent, often daily or weekly.

A hypothetical example: you qualify for $35,000 on a low-doc basis at a 1.28 factor, so $44,800 total payback over about 8 months. A fully documented bank loan might have cost less in total but required a month or more of preparation and could have been declined for thin history. The question is whether the speed and accessibility are worth the difference for your situation. Terms in real offers vary widely.

sections.h2: Prepare your statements to look their best
paragraphs: Because statements are the whole case, a little housekeeping helps. Keep personal and business spending separate so underwriters are not guessing which deposits are revenue. Avoid overdrafts in the months before applying where you can. Be ready to explain large irregular deposits or transfers, and make sure every page of every statement is included in your upload.

If you operate multiple business accounts, offer statements for each, since a partial view can understate revenue. Consistency in the business name across statements and identification also prevents verification delays.

sections.h2: What to confirm before you accept
paragraphs: Light paperwork should not mean light scrutiny on your side. Confirm total payback, payment amount and frequency, fees deducted from proceeds, prepayment terms, and the presence of any personal guarantee, UCC lien or confession of judgment, which is treated differently from state to state. If you do not understand a clause, ask for clarification in writing or consult an attorney.

Fidelity Funding is a broker that connects owners with funding partners, including those that underwrite primarily from bank statements, depending on your profile. A short application, a soft credit pull for the initial review and a specialist who explains each offer can help you see whether low-doc makes sense. Gather your recent statements and start the application when you are ready.

key_takeaways: Low-doc means fewer documents, mainly recent bank statements, not no documents.
Underwriters read deposits, balances, negative days and existing debt payments.
Pricing is generally higher than fully documented bank loans, in exchange for speed and access.
Clean, separated statements are your strongest asset.

faq.q: What documents do low-doc lenders require?
faq.a: Usually three to six months of business bank statements, owner ID and basic business details, sometimes with a voided check or brief call. Requirements vary by funding partner, so confirm the list when you apply. Ask early whether any extra items are needed so nothing stalls review.

Often not for bank-statement-based products. Some partners may still ask for additional documents for larger amounts or to clarify unusual activity. Banks and SBA programs generally do require them. Some partners may still request additional items for larger requests. Every business is different, so a funding specialist can walk through how this applies to your numbers.

Generally, yes. With fewer data points, funders price in more uncertainty, and terms are usually shorter. Compare total payback and payment schedules against any fully documented options you might qualify for. A funding specialist can show you both kinds of offers side by side.

Frequent overdrafts or negative days, inconsistent deposits, heavy existing debt payments and missing statement pages. Mixing personal and business activity also complicates review. Approval is never guaranteed even with strong statements. Clearing up the record before you apply often improves what you are offered.

faq.q: Can a new business use this kind of funding?
faq.a: Some partners work with businesses that have only a few months of statements, provided deposits are steady, though options may be fewer and amounts smaller. A specialist can discuss what is realistic for your time in business. Expect the amount to be modest at first and to grow only as your history does.
